comment: Ruby endless methods without parentheses, like `def to_report = self.class.foo(:@x)`. The builtin Ruby grammar treats everything after `def name ` as an unparenthesized parameter list (`meta.function.method.with-arguments.ruby`) until the end of the line, so method calls in the body are scoped as `meta.function.method ... entity.name.function` and highlighted as definitions, and words like `self` become parameters. This rule matches `def name =` first and scopes it like a method without arguments, so the body is tokenized as regular code. Endless methods with parentheses, like `def foo(a) = a`, are already fine. Remove this when https://github.com/textmate/ruby.tmbundle supports them.

patterns.comment: Same method name pattern as the builtin grammar, without setters (`def x=(v)`), which can not be endless. The `=` must follow whitespace and must not start `==`, `=~` or `=>`
patterns.name: meta.function.method.without-arguments.ruby
